interpretation: Hidden distributional history can be causally relevant to a declared present-state target under one frozen lagged process: 12 of the 45 v24 hidden-age residual rows produced different mature-state maps.
Final occupancy and complete equilibrium source provenance can therefore be identical while present mature/not-yet-mature state differs.
History relevance remains target-specific: six design rows had different first-arrival maps but identical mature-state maps under the frozen two-step lag.
The mature-state target is strictly coarser than complete first-arrival state, and exact activation history can remain unresolved while the present mature-state target is already identified.
Age-dependent present-state memory occurs in both unique-origin and confluence zones, so history dependence is not restricted to source-overlap locations.
claim_boundary: The two-step maturation lag is synthetic and not calibrated to any species.
Mature/not-yet-mature is an abstract present ecological state, not abundance, reproduction, fitness or extinction.
A present-state difference demonstrates possible history dependence under the declared process, not empirical priority effects.
The six age-different but mature-equivalent rows show that hidden history should not be treated as ecologically consequential without a declared target process.
